name: Heun
plain: Predicts with Euler, re-evaluates the model at the landing point, and averages the two slopes. That second call is why it costs about twice as many model calls as Euler for the same step count. Deterministic unless churn is used.
math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
x₂=x+d·dt, dt=σ'−σ̂; D₂=model(x₂,σ'); d₂=(x₂−D₂)/σ'; x'=x+dt·(d+d₂)/2.
Optional churn before the model call (defaults off; no core node exposes s_churn): γ=min(s_churn/N, √2−1) when s_tmin≤σ≤s_tmax, N=len(sigmas)−1; σ̂=σ(1+γ); x←x+ε·s_noise·√(σ̂²−σ²), ε from torch.randn_like (global RNG, not the seeded noise sampler). All later σ in the step are σ̂.

props.stages: 2; 1 when σ'=0 (total 2N−1 if schedule ends in 0)
props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 falls to one Euler step, which equals D.
props.flow_const: No branch; works from d, as in Euler.
